symptom: Moving Src.A1, Src.A2, Src.A3, Src.A4 (an association chain) to Dst in that order: after the second move mx check reported CE9208 (cross-module association Src.A3_A2 and association Dst.A2_A1 'map to the same database table'), and the third move was refused: 'element id(s) are used more than once' held by [Association CrossAssociation] and [DeleteBehavior DeleteBehavior]. Descending order worked.
cause: Moving A2 converts Src.A3_A2 into a cross-association that stays in Src, keeping its $ID. Reconcile's TransplantIDs then aligned Src's CrossAssociations list ([A2_A1] stored, [A3_A2] written) by position and mapped A3_A2's $ID onto A2_A1's; on an mxcli-created model GUID == $ID, so the substitution rewrote the GUID too. Two associations then shared one identity in two units, and the next move brought them into one.
insight: **An element that already carries a stored $ID under the same name is that element; the alignment must not hand it another.** The positional fallback exists so a renamed element keeps its id, but here the written element was not new: its own $ID was in the stored unit, on an Association it had been retyped from, in another list. The pairer now skips such an element and its whole subtree (the delete behaviour under it was the second duplicate). The rule is restricted to named elements: canon's own tests deliberately reuse id values across unnamed flow objects (round-trip, patch control), and those keep the old pairing. The GUID loss is the dangerous half: CLAUDE.md's GUID rule says a changed association GUID drops its table on deploy, and the storage-GUID guard did not see it because it pairs on $ID + Name and the names differed. Live, 11.12.6 blank project: all four ascending moves succeed, every association keeps its original $ID, mx check 0 errors.
